rationale.primary: GRU v2 is the ONLY model with an authoritative downstream navigation evaluation inside the actual 15C EKF + active NHC pipeline (72-case, 4 held-out test sequences). Median FDE 186.26 m vs 250.87 m for GRU v1 (-25.8%), Wilcoxon p=5.1e-5. Wins 50/72, loses 22/72.
rationale.ai_metrics: GRU v2 achieves test RMSE 4.4016 vs TCN-GRU 5.7270 and Transformer 5.4223 — best velocity accuracy on the held-out test set.
rationale.caveat: SIH pass rate (3/72, 4.2%) and heading drift (36.8%) are unchanged vs GRU v1. The navigation bottleneck is heading accuracy, not speed accuracy. GRU v2 reduces median FDE but does not solve the underlying heading problem.
rationale.compute: GRU v2 has 153,729 parameters (exceeds 100k edge budget) and ~604 KB disk. TCN-GRU (17,434 params, 78.6 KB) and Transformer (19,746 params, 125 KB) are both edge-budget eligible and faster on single-CPU inference, but lack authoritative nav evaluation — their nav benefit is unquantified.
rationale.why_not_tcn_or_transformer: Neither TCN-GRU nor Transformer ran through the 72-case 15C+NHC nav evaluation in Steps 16B/16C. Selecting one based on test RMSE alone would be speculation. Decision rule (spec §7): existing downstream nav evidence takes priority over all other criteria.
